display.title: Parshas Shemini: The Two Signs of a Kosher Animal
display.summary_short: Living with the weekly parsha: Uncle Yossi teaches from Parshas Shemini the two signs of a kosher animal, with the pig, the camel and the rabbit as examples.
display.summary_long: A kashrus talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given the week of Parshas Shemini. Uncle Yossi begins with the Alter Rebbe's teaching that we must 'live with the times', which the Mitteler Rebbe explained as living with the weekly parsha, learning a part each day of the week. He opens the Chumash to Shishi of Shemini, where Hashem teaches Moshe Rabbeinu and Aharon HaKohen which animals may be eaten. A kosher animal needs two signs: fully split hooves and chewing its cud, and he explains how a cow or sheep brings up its food to chew again. An animal with only one sign is not kosher: the pig has split hooves but does not chew its cud, while the camel and the rabbit chew their cud but lack split hooves. He concludes that Hashem gave these laws out of love, like a devoted father who tells his only child what is good to eat, because He alone knows what is best for our body and soul.
display.lesson: Hashem gave us the laws of kashrus out of love, because He knows best what is good for our body and soul.
